title: Morocco: Release detained Sahrawi activists and end reprisals against prisoners’ families
content:
CIVICUS calls on the Moroccan authorities to immediately release seven Sahrawi activists arrested during a peaceful gathering in Rabat on 12 October 2026 and to end reprisals against their families and supporters. The gathering was organised in support of Sahrawi prisoners from the Gdeim Izik group, who are on an open-ended hunger strike. Reports of ill-treatment in custody and restrictions on families and supporters seeking to attend court proceedings have heightened concerns about the activists’ safety, due process rights and freedom of peaceful assembly.

Police, supported by auxiliary forces, reportedly used physical force against participants outside the General Delegation for Prison Administration and Reintegration.They then arrested seven activists; Hassana Douihi, Salah Eddine Sabbar, Brahim Babit, Mohamed Mrabet, Khalid Boufriwa, El Houssein Chihab and Aziz El Ouahidi. Transliteration of some names varies across sources.

On 14 October, after about 48 hours in custody, the seven activists were brought before the public prosecutor. They reportedly face allegations including participation in an unauthorised gathering and violence against public security personnel.
